content.value_statement: Teams need commit messages that are consistent, searchable, and linked to the right issues. This skill formats changes using Sentry conventions for subjects, bodies, footers, and reverts.
actual_capabilities: Applies the Sentry commit structure with type, optional scope, subject, body, and footer.
Selects supported commit types such as feat, fix, ref, docs, test, chore, and perf.
Formats issue footers with Fixes or Refs for GitHub, Sentry, and Linear identifiers.
Produces messages for simple fixes, features, refactors, breaking changes, and reverts.
Keeps subjects aligned with imperative wording, no final period, and the 70-character limit.
limitations: Does not run git commands or inspect repository history.
Requires the user to provide change details and issue identifiers.
Focuses on Sentry conventions, not every team-specific commit style.
Does not verify whether referenced issues exist or should close.

use_cases.title: Prepare focused commits
use_cases.description: Turn a short change summary into a Sentry-style commit message with the correct type, scope, and footer.

use_cases.title: Review commit history
use_cases.description: Rewrite vague commit messages into consistent subjects and bodies before merging a pull request.

use_cases.title: Document release changes
use_cases.description: Create clear messages that preserve issue references and highlight breaking changes for later release notes.

prompt_templates.title: Basic commit message
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for one clear message.
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Sentry-style commit message for this change: [describe change]. Include a type, subject, and optional body.

prompt_templates.title: Add issue reference
prompt_templates.scenario: Message needs a closing or linking footer.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Sentry-style commit message for [change summary]. Use [Fixes or Refs] with issue [issue ID] in the footer.

prompt_templates.title: Choose the commit type
prompt_templates.scenario: User is unsure whether the change is a fix, feature, refactor, or maintenance task.
prompt_templates.prompt: Choose the best Sentry commit type for this change and write the message: [change details]. Explain the type choice briefly.

prompt_templates.title: Review multiple options
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for comparing candidate messages.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft three Sentry-style commit messages for this change summary: [details]. Recommend the strongest option and explain why it fits.

output_examples.input: A bug fix prevents the user API from crashing when deleted accounts return no data.
output_examples.output: Suggested subject: fix(api): Handle missing deleted-account data. The body should explain the null response and why the guard is needed.

output_examples.input: A feature adds Slack thread replies for alert updates and should link to GH-1234 without closing it.
output_examples.output: Suggested subject: feat(alerts): Add Slack thread replies for updates. Use a Refs footer for GH-1234 because the issue should remain open.

output_examples.input: A breaking API change removes deprecated v1 endpoints and closes SENTRY-9999.
output_examples.output: Suggested subject: feat(api)!: Remove deprecated v1 endpoints. Include a breaking change note and a Fixes footer for SENTRY-9999.

best_practices: Provide one focused change and any relevant issue IDs before asking for a message.
Use Fixes only when the merge should close the referenced issue.
Keep the subject short and use the body for motivation and previous behavior.
anti_patterns: Mixing unrelated changes into one commit message.
Ending the subject with punctuation or using past tense.
Adding issue footers without knowing whether they should close the issue.

faq.question: Does this skill run git commit?
faq.answer: No. It only helps write commit message text and does not execute git commands.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is marked for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Which issue formats does it support?
faq.answer: It documents GitHub numbers, GH identifiers, Sentry issue IDs, and Linear issue IDs.

faq.question: Can it write breaking change messages?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the removed behavior, migration impact, and issue ID when available.

faq.question: Can it adapt to non-Sentry conventions?
faq.answer: It can help with general conventional commits, but its rules are centered on Sentry conventions.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No. The skill includes a documentation link, but it does not require network access to work.
